title: Objective
description: A funded, checkable question. The record's SHA-256 over its canonical serialization IS its id, so the verifier block is part of the objective's identity: editing an evaluator forks the objective rather than rescoring work already done against it.

goal.description: Identifier of the parent goal this objective decomposes.

statement.description: What is being asked, in prose, precisely enough that the verifier is recognisably a faithful encoding of it.

verifier.$comment: Per-kind fields are validated by the verifier itself, which returns INVALID_SPEC rather than a settling verdict when the spec is malformed.

reward.description: Integer units of account. Never a float -- floats do not round-trip identically across implementations.

ratchet.description: Progressive-bounty parameters. When present the objective pays along an improvement curve instead of once to a single winner. Part of the id, like the verifier.
ratchet.$comment: Field shape is validated by frontier::Ratchet, which reports a malformed block rather than settling on it.

confidentiality.description: When settled artifacts become public -- never whether. Omitted or null means 'public', and writing it explicitly produces byte-identical output, so this field did not reissue any pre-existing objective id. 'sealed' is declared so its cost is explicit but is refused at validation: paying for an artifact nobody may read requires a zero-knowledge proof that the pinned verifier accepts it, which is not implemented. Use 'embargoed' for delayed disclosure.

embargo_epochs.description: How many epochs an embargoed artifact stays shut after its commitment's epoch closes. Meaningful only with confidentiality 'embargoed', and refused on anything else rather than ignored -- a funder who thinks they asked for delay and did not is the failure they cannot see. Zero is refused for the same reason: an artifact readable in the epoch after its commitment is on the normal reveal schedule, which is what 'public' already means. Inside the objective's id when present, so an embargo cannot be shortened after work has started; omitted when absent, so adding it reissued nothing. Enforced where it can be: a committee share is what opens a sealed artifact, so a share published before the embargo lifts is refused by both implementations. An embargoed objective with no length is legal and unenforced -- that is the shape the class had when it was a label nothing checked.
embargo_epochs.$comment: The presence of the number is what turns enforcement on, the same shape as the issuance record turning supply accounting on.

artifact_schema.description: What shape of artifact the verifier expects, for a submitter who has only this record. Documentation, not a rule: nothing validates an artifact against it, because the pinned verifier is the only thing that decides what passes and a second gate would be a second answer to that question. It exists because an agent's only other source for the artifact's shape is the statement, which is attacker-authored prose. Part of the id like every other field; omitted when absent, so adding it reissued nothing.
artifact_schema.$comment: Deliberately unconstrained beyond 'an object'. Requiring JSON Schema here would make this crate's validator the arbiter of a field the funder writes, and a funder whose hint is a worked example rather than a schema is being more helpful, not less.

require_signed_submitter.description: Refuse submissions from anyone but a signed identity. When true, a submitter must be 64 lowercase hex characters -- an ed25519 public key -- and the record must carry a signature from it. Omitted when false, which is what every objective written before this field existed meant.
